title: A Cozy look at A Traveler's Guide: Inns & Taverns; and Downtime in Zyan
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7tKbMZqzLks

Daniel (@dungeondive) opens 2023 with two zines he calls cozy, and the pairing is smarter than it first looks: one furnishes the tavern, the other gives your characters a reason to stay in it.

A Traveler's Guide: Inns & Taverns is by Madeline Hale, author of the Table Fables books, and Daniel found it on itch.io on Christmas morning, printed it on card stock and read it by the tree. It holds ten fully detailed taverns plus generators for building your own. Each entry gives the exterior, the barkeep, the notable patrons, a d6 encounter table, lodging prices and a menu — and Daniel is candid that the menus made him hungry. The detail he keeps returning to is that adventure hooks are seeded through the descriptions rather than listed: a shy patron nursing mulled wine turns out to be hunting a mushroom thought extinct. Part two runs names, cleanliness, lighting, atmosphere and a d100 quirk table.

Downtime in Zyan, by Ben Lawrence, gamifies what happens between adventures — building institutions, cultivating relationships, gathering intelligence, spellcraft, spiritual exercises and, his favourite, revelry. Each runs on a tracker where progress can slip backwards; the institution tracker climbs from inconsequential to legendary, with a growing-pains table that can drop you a step. His verdict ties the two together: this only looks like downtime, and each subsystem plants seeds for the next adventure.

----

Daniel says downtime is only worth tracking when it isn't really downtime — when it generates hooks. Where's the line for you between meaningful between-adventure play and bookkeeping you'd rather skip?
